scope.runtime_reason: No narrow positive original trace was available in the permitted corpus. Historical runtime evidence did not reach a resource hit/miss/open/release sequence, so runtime identity is not promoted.

question: What is the stable resource identity, how do DBPF, manager registries, caches, Cell serializer references, leases, and runtime objects differ, and what provider/cache semantics are safe to freeze?

executive_resolution.conceptual_identity: Manager/provider content requests use the full numeric ResourceKey triple (instanceID, typeID, groupID). Cell local cCellDataReference_ lookup is a separate (instanceID, serializer*) pair identity, not a manager/provider request key.
executive_resolution.architecture_decision: Keep the manager/provider ResourceKey, Cell local pair identity, representation order, package order, cache identity, lease/reference state, and runtime object identity as separate layers. Do not flatten them into one global map or one pointer identity.
executive_resolution.minimum_provider_cache_contract: Manager/provider requests carry a full numeric ResourceKey. Cell local cCellDataReference_ lookup uses (instanceID, serializer*) and is outside that provider contract. Cache entries, record leases, and runtime objects remain separate identities; the provider returns a value/record/resource outcome without promising a particular runtime object or DBPF row order.

hypotheses.name: single_global_identity
hypotheses.claim: One identity value is incorrectly treated as the contract for every layer: the full numeric ResourceKey is the manager/provider request identity, while the Cell local cCellDataReference_ list uses (instanceID, serializer*) and cache, lease, and runtime object identities are separate.
predictions: Every layer would compare or hash the same instance/type/group triple.
A Cell reference would search by the full ResourceKey rather than by a serializer pointer.
A ResourceObject pointer would not be independently meaningful from its mNameKey.
evidence_for: ResourceKey is the manager and database content contract.
DatabasePackedFile stores a map<ResourceKey, PFRecordBase*> at +0x2e8.
ResourceObject embeds a ResourceKey at +0x08.
evidence_against: cCellDataReference_::Create at 0x00e82420 searches only instanceID and serializer pointer, not typeID or groupID.
ICache methods receive a ResourceKey, but the returned object is a separate pointer and reference-counted object.
The record lease is an IRecord/open-count object, not a ResourceKey.
hypotheses.independence: The manager/database structures, Cell list body, cache vtable calls, and lease APIs are independent evidence streams.
hypotheses.repetition: The full triple repeats across manager and database layers; repetition confirms the content contract but does not erase the Cell pair or runtime pointer distinctions.

hypotheses.name: layered_identity
hypotheses.claim: Manager/provider requests use the stable full numeric ResourceKey, while Cell local cCellDataReference_ lookup intentionally uses the separate (instanceID, serializer*) pair; representation, database, factory, cache, lease, and runtime-object identities remain separate layers with explicit translation or ownership boundaries.
predictions: Memory key order, DBPF row order, and serializer order can differ without changing conceptual equality.
Database priority and cache registration order can select a provider independently of key ordering.
A Cell serializer pointer can identify a local Cell reference entry, but it does not replace the full ResourceKey in manager/provider requests; the loaded cCellResource retains its own mNameKey.
evidence_for: ResourceKey memory layout is instance/type/group; DBPF rows are type/group/instance.
Manager mappings at +0x54 and +0x78 translate resource type to record type and back.
Database list insertion and FindDatabase traversal are priority ordered.
ICache and cCellDataReference_ expose different key contracts and lifetimes.
evidence_against: The exact public semantics of some SDK/live address aliases remain boundary-sensitive.
Runtime hit/miss, async, and rekey behavior were not observed.
hypotheses.independence: The conclusion combines direct layouts, vtable bytes, map/list algorithms, and independent Cell lifecycle bodies; it is not a single narrative source.
hypotheses.repetition: The same layered distinction is visible in several APIs, but repeated API naming is not counted as independent runtime proof.

hypotheses.name: cache_key_is_runtime_object
hypotheses.claim: The report conflates manager/provider request identity with Cell-local and runtime identities by treating a runtime ResourceObject pointer or Cell reference node as the manager/provider key.
predictions: ICache::GetResource would receive or compare an object pointer rather than a key.
A cache miss would be defined by a new object address even when the numeric key is equal.
cCellDataReference_ would be an alias for the manager cache rather than a separate local list.
evidence_for: The manager stores cache implementations and returns ResourceObject handles.
ResourceObject and Cell data references are intrusive/reference-counted.
evidence_against: ICache::GetResource and CacheResource use ResourceKey/ResourceObject metadata, and the manager supports an alternate pCacheName.
0x00e82420 maintains a separate global circular list keyed by instance and serializer.
0x00e82280 and 0x00e823e0 release local resource pointers independently of manager cache traversal.
hypotheses.independence: The cache vtable contract, manager cache traversal, and Cell list lifecycle are separate bodies and structures.
hypotheses.repetition: Pointer use in return values is not repeated as proof of pointer-keyed lookup; the key-bearing call contracts are the separator.

hypotheses.name: dbpf_row_order_is_identity
hypotheses.claim: The order of rows in a DBPF index defines conceptual resource identity and duplicate-key precedence.
predictions: Changing only the DBPF row order would change the resource identity or its canonical key.
DatabasePackedFile would expose raw row order rather than a key map.
Cross-package precedence would be irrelevant if the first row in one package always won.
evidence_for: The current OpenSpore parser scans one package's index in file order and returns the first exact T:G:I match.
DBPF rows contain a concrete serialized order.
evidence_against: DatabasePackedFile has an explicit map<ResourceKey, PFRecordBase*> at +0x2e8.
The original manager has a priority-sorted database list and a first-match database traversal.
The SDK ResourceKey equality is a numeric triple comparison, not a row-position comparison.
hypotheses.independence: The current parser is a separate implementation comparison; the original map and database-list algorithms are independent Ghidra evidence.
hypotheses.repetition: Repeated first-match observations in one package describe enumeration behavior, not conceptual identity or multi-package precedence.

hypotheses.name: one_global_provider
hypotheses.claim: A single global provider owns package bytes, factories, caches, Cell references, and runtime objects.
predictions: All record lookup would bypass separate database/factory/cache layers.
Cell data references would call the same global cache and expose the same object identity.
Database priority and cache registration would not be architecture-visible.
evidence_for: cResourceManager is a global service with registries and a vtable.
Many gameplay consumers eventually reach resource APIs.
evidence_against: cResourceManager fields separately expose database, factory, type-mapping, cache, and filename registries.
DatabasePackedFile owns the package index and record lease operations.
cCellDataReference_ owns a separate lazy reference list and serializer-specific loading path.
hypotheses.independence: The manager constructor/fields, database structures, Cell list, and cache vtable are independent ownership evidence.
hypotheses.repetition: The manager's central fan-in establishes a coordination role, not ownership of every layer.

hypotheses.name: runtime_object_is_content_identity
hypotheses.claim: The runtime ResourceObject pointer is the durable content identity and can replace the numeric key.
predictions: Equal numeric keys always return the same object pointer.
A private/reload request can be represented solely by replacing the pointer.
The embedded mNameKey is redundant or ignored for lookup.
evidence_for: Runtime consumers receive pointer handles and use Cast/AddRef/Release operations.
evidence_against: ResourceObject embeds mNameKey at +0x08 and is reference-counted.
The SDK exposes private acquisition, reload, cache lookup, and separate cache identity overrides.
cCellDataReference_ stores an intrusive cCellResource pointer separately from its instance/serializer key.
hypotheses.independence: The object layout, manager acquisition surfaces, and Cell pointer lifecycle are separate from the key-bearing database/cache operations.
hypotheses.repetition: Repeated pointer returns are evidence of runtime handles, not proof of pointer-based content identity.

package_precedence.static_rule: FUN_008de940 stores database pointer at node+4 and priority at node+8, then inserts before the first node whose priority is lower than the new priority. Equal priorities are traversed and therefore remain after existing equal entries.
package_precedence.lookup_rule: The database list is traversed in list order; the first database whose record lookup/open operation succeeds wins. An explicit database override bypasses the global list.
package_precedence.record_mapping_rule: 0x008df9b0 first consults the manager resource-type-to-record-type mapping at +0x54, then calls the database path; on success it can write the corrected real record key to pDst.
package_precedence.factory_rule: 0x008dfb20 walks the resource factory map and returns the first factory whose CanConvert(resourceType, recordType) succeeds; wildcard record type is represented by the special -1 path.
package_precedence.runtime_status: Static priority/list behavior is supported as a provisional model; actual boot registration order and duplicate content selection remain provisional pending runtime evidence.

cell_reference_resolution.create: 0x00e82420 searches by (instanceID, serializer), calls 0x00e82340 on a miss, links the new 24-byte node into DAT_016b44f0, and returns node+8.
cell_reference_resolution.allocation_helper: 0x00e82340 allocates exactly 0x18 bytes, copies the 16-byte payload to node+0x08, retains a non-null resource pointer, and returns the node base. It is not an alias of Create.
cell_reference_resolution.lazy_load: 0x00e823a0 increments the payload counter, calls 0x00e822c0 if the resource pointer is null, then uses the resource object/Cast path to expose the data.
cell_reference_resolution.failure_and_release: 0x00e822c0 releases an existing pointer, attempts the asset/mode load gate, logs failure through 0x00e84e40, and releases/cleans the pointer on failure. 0x00e82280 releases all live payload resource pointers while retaining nodes; 0x00e823e0 releases and frees nodes during teardown.
cell_reference_resolution.identity_conclusion: The Cell list is a local lazy-reference cache keyed by instanceID plus serializer, not a manager ICache and not a full ResourceKey. The underlying cCellResource retains its own mNameKey and serializer.

cache_and_request_trace.request_key_contract: All manager/provider request surfaces use the full numeric ResourceKey. Cell local cCellDataReference_::Create is not a manager/provider request and uses (instanceID, serializer*) for its local list lookup. Manager cache, record lease, and runtime object identities remain separate from both.
normal_request_shape: On a hit, the existing resource handle is returned without a package record load.
On a miss, manager mapping and database selection are attempted.
The selected database/factory path opens a record and constructs a ResourceObject/cCellResource.
The manager may insert the result into a cache through CacheResource.
cache_and_request_trace.common_loader: 0x008df0b0 contains the same database/factory/record-construction family and is reached by the short 0x008df430 wrapper; the exact SDK anchor 0x008df700 is an interior label of the rebounded 0x008df460 body.
cache_and_request_trace.cache_key_override: The SDK GetResource surface accepts pCacheName; when supplied it is the cache identity, while the requested name remains the content lookup identity. No evidence shows that pCacheName changes the DBPF record key.
invalidations: SDK interfaces expose GetPrivateResource, ReloadResource, CacheResource, FlushCache, and database-change notification.
0x008de400 invokes ICache::Flush on one cache or all caches.
The Cell local list has independent clear/destroy paths at 0x00e82280, 0x00e823e0, and 0x00e824d0.
Exact manager cache replacement during ReloadResource and exact release timing after Flush remain unresolved.

adversarial_steps.name: one-global-identity-collapse-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A single full ResourceKey comparison would be sufficient in the Cell list, cache, record lease, and runtime object.
evidence_for: ResourceKey is consistently embedded in ResourceObject and used by manager/database APIs.
DatabasePackedFile has an explicit ResourceKey map.
evidence_against: 0x00e82420 compares only instanceID and serializer pointer.
ICache calls are key-based but return separate object pointers.
Database OpenRecord returns a record lease rather than the key itself.
adversarial_steps.independence: The contradiction comes from a different Cell list algorithm and separate cache/lease contracts, not from re-reading the manager narrative.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Full-triple use is repeated in manager/database code, but the pair-based Cell hit is a direct counterexample.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Global identity collapse rejected; the stable full triple is only the conceptual content identity.

adversarial_steps.name: global-versus-layered-provider-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A global provider would own the package index, factory, cache, Cell reference, and runtime object without translation boundaries.
evidence_for: cResourceManager is a global coordination service with a 38-slot vtable.
Many consumers reach resource APIs through manager calls.
evidence_against: cResourceManager has separate database, factory, type-mapping, cache, and filename fields.
DatabasePackedFile owns the index and record operations.
cCellDataReference_ has a separate global list and lazy loader.
adversarial_steps.independence: Manager fields, database structure, Cell list, and cache vector are independent owner evidence.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Manager fan-in is coordination evidence, not ownership proof.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Layered providers are supported; a single global provider is rejected.

adversarial_steps.name: dbpf-order-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Changing DBPF row order would change conceptual identity or global duplicate precedence.
evidence_for: The current OpenSpore provider is a first-match linear scan of one parsed index.
evidence_against: DatabasePackedFile stores a ResourceKey map at +0x2e8.
The manager's database list is priority ordered independently of row order.
ResourceKey equality is full-field numeric equality.
adversarial_steps.independence: Current parser behavior and original database/list mechanics are independent implementation paths.
adversarial_steps.repetition: First-match behavior is not repeated as evidence that row order is identity.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: DBPF order is serialization/enumeration infrastructure; key equality and database priority are authoritative.

adversarial_steps.name: resourcekey-memory-order-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: The conceptual triple may be serialized or compared in a different field order without becoming a different content identity.
evidence_for: Ghidra ResourceKey layout is instance/type/group.
DBPF standard row order is type/group/instance.
The SDK ResourceKey operator< compares instance, type, then group.
evidence_against: A raw byte comparison without field-aware decoding would be architecture-specific and unsafe.
adversarial_steps.independence: The Ghidra structure, SDK operator, and DBPF reader are separate sources.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The repeated triple is semantic equivalence, not permission to flatten byte layouts.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Conceptual identity is field-aware and representation order is explicit.

adversarial_steps.name: serializer-versus-key-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: Cell local reference lookup can use (instanceID, serializer*) as its pair identity, while manager/provider requests continue to use the full numeric ResourceKey; the loaded cCellResource still carries mNameKey.
evidence_for: 0x00e82420 searches the list by instanceID and serializer only.
cCellDataReference_ payload stores serializer, intrusive cCellResource, and counter.
cCellResource embeds mNameKey and mDataSerializer.
evidence_against: The serializer pointer is process-address identity and does not describe group or package precedence.
The same instance with different serializer pointers must not be assumed to share a local node.
adversarial_steps.independence: The Create loop, node copy helper, and cCellResource layout are independent bodies/structures.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Serializer use in typed Create wrappers supports the type-discriminator role but does not prove global type identity.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Cell local identity is (instance, serializer); manager identity remains the full triple.

adversarial_steps.name: cache-key-versus-lease-reference-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: A cache hit should be keyed by ResourceKey, while an open record and a ResourceObject are separately owned runtime handles.
evidence_for: ICache::GetResource/CacheResource take ResourceKey/ResourceObject contracts.
0x008de280, 0x008de360, and 0x008de3b0 iterate caches by key and return the first hit/success.
DatabasePackedFile OpenRecord and PFRecordRead expose record/stream state separate from ResourceKey.
evidence_against: The same object pointer can be returned through an intrusive reference and may outlive a particular record lease.
A pointer address is not a stable package identity.
adversarial_steps.independence: Cache traversal, database OpenRecord, and object refcount layout are separate evidence paths.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Multiple cache call sites repeat key-bearing lookup, not pointer identity.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Cache key, record lease, and runtime object identity are separate; pointer equality cannot replace key semantics.

adversarial_steps.name: package-precedence-separator
adversarial_steps.prediction: A higher-priority database should be inserted before a lower-priority database, and FindDatabase/FindRecord should select the first successful database in that order.
evidence_for: 0x008de940 stores database and priority in list nodes and inserts before the first lower-priority node.
0x008de310 traverses the database list in order and tests the record path.
0x008df9b0 supports an explicit database override and otherwise uses the manager database path.
evidence_against: Boot registration order and actual duplicate-record hits were not runtime-observed.
Equal-priority behavior is static from insertion traversal, not a dynamic event trace.
adversarial_steps.independence: The insertion comparator and consumer traversal are separate function bodies.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same ordering rule is visible in register/find, but repetition does not replace a runtime event trace.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Static insertion and traversal support a provisional descending-priority model; runtime package precedence, duplicate selection, and boot order remain provisional.

adversarial_steps.name: cell-hit-miss-and-invalidation-separator
adversarial_steps.prediction: Create(instance, serializer) should return the same embedded node on a pair hit, allocate/relink on a miss, and lazy-load only when the payload resource pointer is null.
evidence_for: 0x00e82420 has an explicit pair-match branch and a miss path calling 0x00e82340.
0x00e82340 allocates 0x18 bytes and copies the 16-byte payload.
0x00e823a0 increments the counter and calls 0x00e822c0 when mpResource is null.
0x00e82280 and 0x00e823e0 distinguish resource release from node destruction.
evidence_against: No live process was available to observe pointer values, counters, or release timing.
The manager cache and Cell list can both be active, so a Cell hit does not prove a manager cache hit.
adversarial_steps.independence: The Create branch, allocator size, lazy-load branch, and teardown bodies are separate static separators.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same pair key is repeated in two Create callers, which confirms reuse shape but not runtime object identity.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Static hit/miss/open/release separator completed. Cell local cache semantics are supported independently of manager cache semantics.

adversarial_steps.name: architecture-dependency-and-runtime-test
adversarial_steps.prediction: The semantic layering should survive a provider replacement, but concrete x86 offsets, pointer serializer identity, vtable slots, and package registration order are binary-specific and require a narrow runtime trace before compatibility promotion.
evidence_for: The value triple and explicit provider layers can be represented without the original classes.
The current B1 provider already fetches one package by the full triple while omitting original manager orchestration.
Runtime identity and exact invalidation are not proven by static bodies.
evidence_against: The current B1 path has one borrowed package, reparses its index per fetch, and has no manager/database/factory/cache layer.
The original binary is x86 32-bit with vtable and pointer-based serializer identity.
adversarial_steps.independence: The architecture test compares the current clean-room seam with original static layers and separately checks historical runtime availability.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The current provider and historical reports are corroboration, not a second original runtime observation.

exact_decisions.decision: Use the full (instanceID,typeID,groupID) triple as the conceptual content identity; expose it field-aware.
Keep ResourceKey memory order (instance,type,group) distinct from DBPF row order (type,group,instance).
Model package/database/provider selection as a layered resolver with an explicit priority/override boundary; freeze only the static list policy and keep runtime package precedence provisional.
Apply resource-type to record-type mapping before database/factory lookup and permit the resolved real key to differ from the requested key.
Keep manager cache identity key-based and separate from the Cell local pair, record leases, and runtime object pointers; treat eviction/release timing as provisional.
Preserve cCellDataReference_ as a separate lazy local-reference layer keyed by instanceID+serializer; 0x00e82340 is its allocator/helper and 0x00e82420 is Create.
Do not use package path, DBPF row position, vtable address, serializer pointer, or ResourceObject pointer as durable content identity.
Treat ReloadResource, GetPrivateResource, FlushCache, and Cell local clear/destroy as explicit lifecycle operations; do not infer same-object reuse or replacement without a trace.
Keep the current OpenSpore B1 boundary as a one-package exact-T:G:I byte provider; do not claim original manager/cache parity from it.
